summary.headline: India Pesticides Q2 FY27 revenue fell 22% YoY to INR 231 crores and PAT to INR 18 crores, while management guides to roughly flat FY26 revenue.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue declined 22% YoY to INR 231 crores, with EBITDA of INR 33 crores (14.4% margin vs 18.2%) and PAT of INR 18 crores (vs INR 32 crores). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 487 crores, down 15.9%, with export revenue at INR 177 crores vs INR 229 crores. Management cited geopolitical disruption, deficient monsoon rains, softer overseas herbicide demand and higher job-work and employee costs. Management says export orders for the coming quarter have been received and aims to make up H1 shortfall in H2, targeting revenue at least equal to FY26.

segments.name: Technicals and API
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 115 crores. Management said the company is about 75% backward integrated and has started indigenous production of the herbicide intermediate Pretilachlor, with imports largely stopped.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 111 crores, up from INR 72 crores in the prior quarter. Management said the figure includes bulk formulation exports, but formulation share still rose YoY after excluding incremental bulk sales.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 export revenue was INR 177 crores vs INR 229 crores a year earlier. New approvals in UK (insecticide, technical equivalence) and Argentina (herbicide) were received; Argentina is expected to add INR 20-25 crores in year one.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to deliver revenue at least equal to FY26 for the full year, with H2 similar to or slightly better than H2 FY26 to partly recover H1 shortfall.
Management is confident of maintaining Q2's 14.4% EBITDA margin going forward.
Export orders of about INR 100 crores from Europe and Australia were cited, partly executed and partly to be executed in coming months.
Subsidiary Hamirpur (Shalvis) stabilisation expected to add INR 40-50 crores turnover in H2 FY27; asset turn of 2 targeted next year, implying at least INR 80 crores additional revenue.
Standalone capex guidance INR 40-45 crores on track; subsidiary capex revised to INR 80-90 crores from earlier INR 120-130 crores combined guidance; inventory expected to normalise by Q4 FY27.
Eight products in pipeline for registrations in Australia, Europe, Brazil and Canada.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at Dewa Road and Sandila: 28,300 MT technicals and 10,200 MT formulations.
Hamirpur (subsidiary): 2 of 10 planned blocks operational; 2 more blocks expected early next year. Permitted capacity 30,000 MT technicals and 6,000 MT formulations.
September 2026 capitalisation of blocks in subsidiary of about INR 65 crores; PPE rose from INR 360 crores to INR 424 crores, CWIP closed at INR 25 crores.
Management is revisiting the Hamirpur product portfolio due to geopolitical and raw material conditions; plant is multipurpose, so products can be swapped with minor changes.
Next year capex to step up again per management.
demand_pricing: Deficient and erratic monsoon in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, parts of Punjab and Haryana reduced herbicide application and affected Kharif crops.
Raw material sourcing: more than 65% from India, about 20% from China, remainder from other countries; supply chain, raw material price volatility and freight were key challenges.
Gross margin around 50% in Q2, higher YoY on product mix; job-work charges rose to about INR 12 crores from INR 6 crores, which would lower gross margin by about 3 points if adjusted.
Customers in more than 35 countries and over 60 international customers, including multinational agrochemical companies.
Argentina is a fresh market with no prior business; UK sales will be through existing customers under letters of access. EU sales are via formulators only.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for EBITDA margins if the war continues over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of maintaining the Q2 EBITDA margin; raw material is more than 65% India-sourced and about 20% from China.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new export orders and can they drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders are a mix of technical and bulk formulation (WDG and EC) for existing molecules, covering Europe and Australia, with about INR 100 crores in size; management expects to cover the H1 shortfall in the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected business from the UK and Argentina approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Argentina is expected to contribute INR 20-25 crores in the first year from one molecule, with a second molecule registration in progress; UK business is expected from existing customers in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise and what drove the formulation jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Job-work charges rose to about INR 12 crores from INR 6 crores as an intermediate moved to job work; formulation growth partly reflected bulk exports but formulation share rose YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why is subsidiary capex lower than earlier guidance and why are products changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary capex is now INR 80-90 crores vs earlier guidance; the Hamirpur product mix is being revisited due to geopolitics, with the same plant able to run both products.

risks_watch: H1 revenue and exports down about 16% and 23%; delivery of the INR 100 crore export order book and whether FY26 revenue is matched.
Gross margin pressure from job-work charges (about INR 12 crores in Q2) and higher employee costs; lower forex income reduced EBITDA.
Current tax true-up: about INR 15 crores provided and INR 9 crores paid in H1, with a balance to be paid next quarter.
Hamirpur product portfolio revision could delay or change the expansion ramp-up and asset turn targets.
Inventory build from a deferred export order and a rice herbicide with lower Q1 sales; management expects normalisation by Q4 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on demand and geopolitics, but confident on near-term export orders and margin maintenance. Management was direct on the H1 revenue shortfall, while answers on product portfolio changes and tax provisioning were less precise.
key_quotes: Overseas demand for our herbicide also remains softer with export revenue of INR 177 crores during H1 FY27.
we are quite confident that we should be able to maintain the EBITDA margin what we have achieved in this quarter.
Whatever we are lagging in half year, at least we want to cover this up in the coming 6 months.
We are anticipating at least first year, INR 20 crores, INR 25 crores.

adds.what: Hamirpur subsidiary: 2 more of 10 planned blocks expected early next year (permitted 30,000 MT technicals and 6,000 MT formulations)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue at least equal to FY26 (qualitative, implies H2 recovery after H1 down 15.9%), backed by ~INR 100 crore Europe/Australia export orders, Argentina approval (INR 20-25 crore year one), and Hamirpur subsidiary adding INR 40-50 crore in H2 with 2 more blocks early next year, but no hard numbers for the full-year target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is confident of holding the Q2 EBITDA margin of 14.4% (vs 18.2% a year ago), but that is a hold at a lower level, not an expansion, with job-work costs of about INR 12 crores vs INR 6 crores weighing on gross margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hamirpur subsidiary has 2 of 10 blocks running, about INR 65 crores capitalised in September 2026, and 2 more blocks expected early next year, though the product portfolio is being revisited.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue fell 15.9% to INR 487 crores, but about INR 100 crores of Europe/Australia export orders and Hamirpur adding INR 40-50 crores in H2 are meant to bring H2 to at least similar to H2 FY26 and full-year revenue to at least FY26 levels.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says next year's capex will step up again, and utilisation is not disclosed, so a new capex plan is likely but without a firm date or amount.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is only to maintain last year's revenue level, H1 is down 15.9%, and the H2 recovery depends on delivering the export orders.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue is down 15.9% and exports down about 23%, the FY26 revenue target needs a strong H2 recovery, and the Hamirpur portfolio revision could delay the ramp-up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Eight products are in the pipeline for registrations in Australia, Europe, Brazil and Canada, and Argentina adds a second molecule with registration in progress.

rows.label: Argentina herbicide approval contributes INR 20-25 crores in year one
rows.why: The Argentina approval is a fresh market with no prior business, and management expects INR 20-25 crores in the first year from one molecule.

rows.label: Europe and Australia export orders of about INR 100 crores
rows.why: The order book is partly executed and partly to be executed in coming months, and management expects it to cover the H1 shortfall within six months.

rows.label: Hamirpur subsidiary stabilisation
rows.why: Management expects INR 40-50 crores of turnover in H2 FY27 and asset turn of 2 next year, implying at least INR 80 crores of additional revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on the export order book and holding the 14.4% EBITDA margin, and cautious on demand, monsoon and geopolitics; analysts pressed on the H1 shortfall, the Hamirpur product changes and tax provisioning, where answers were less precise.
